correctness.rationale: Strict substochasticity gives nonnegative G=(I-Lambda W)^(-1), h=G e_i>=0, and h_i=max_v h_v>=1 by the maximum principle. A changed row is rank one, hence z(S)=z+alpha(S)h. Resolvent substitution gives alpha=lambda_i sum_{j in S}(z_j-b_i)/(d_i+|S|h_i-lambda_i sum_{j in S}h_j) with denominator >=d_i+|S|(1-lambda_i)h_i>0. Thus one optimal alpha yields coordinatewise domination of every other feasible outcome, making every nondecreasing aggregate objective optimal simultaneously, without claiming identical sets of *all* optimizers. At each fixed k, fractional-programming optimality at t=r makes maximizers of sum_{j in S}(z_j+t h_j) attain the optimal ratio; these top k selections change only at O(m^2) pairwise affine-score crossings. Including crossing points, intervals, k=1..K and empty set returns the exact optimum in polynomial bit/arithmetic time. The 4-node rational example reverses the raw opinion ordering (gain 27/1450>1251/82550). Independent exact matrix inversions and enumeration of all eligible subsets of this example passed.

value.rationale: The directed-FJ structural median optimization is hard when receiver tails vary. A practical natural one-receiver intervention class admits a surprising universal exact order on whole equilibria and an executable polynomial-time discrete optimizer for every quantile, mean and threshold, plus an exact counterexample to naive highest-baseline-donor ranking.

limitations: One prescribed receiver only, uniformly normalized new and old row edges, strict 0<lambda_v<1, no self loops and nonempty neighborhoods.
Real-world adoption of edges is outside the mathematical intervention model.
Does not classify all optimal sets for each monotone statistic, merely supplies one universally dominating optimizer.
